slides.title: Toward Geometry-Scalable Whole-Body Touch for Humanoids: A 3D-Printed Conformal EIT Skin
slides.highlight: This work introduces a conformal electrical impedance tomography skin that reduces redesign burdens for humanoid tactile coverage, supporting the RwB goal of developing embodied social robots for contact-rich human environments.

card.one_liner: A 3D-printed, conformal EIT tactile skin for scalable contact localization on curved humanoid surfaces.
card.key_idea: Combines a conductive TPU sensing layer with low-resistance contact-enhancement patches, using a Gauss–Newton EIT solver to reconstruct conductivity changes from boundary voltage measurements.
card.evaluation: Tested on planar, U-shaped, and iCub-face geometries. The curved sensor achieved a 6mm mean localization error over 18 positions without supervised post-processing.
card.limitation: Requires manual assembly of electrodes and conductive patches; force response is non-linear and requires calibration for accurate estimation.

slides.title: ReTouch: Empowering Contact-Rich Dexterous Manipulation with Online-Refined Tactile Prediction
slides.tldr: VLA MODEL FOR CONTACT-RICH DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: ReTouch introduces a vision-language-action model that uses a Tactile-Patch Encoder and a high-frequency action module to refine tactile predictions online, improving robustness in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: ReTouch improves contact-rich dexterous manipulation by online-refining future tactile predictions and action chunks using feedback.
card.key_idea: A VLA framework using a Tactile-Patch Encoder for structured finger-wise representations and a Foresight Action Expert to recursively update tactile latents and actions during execution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on XHT-Dataset (900 demonstrations, 7 tasks) using XHand–UR7e; outperformed strongest baselines by 18.4% (standard) and 23.8% (challenging) in success rate.

slides.title: TWINS: A Tactile Wearable Isomorphic Arm Networked System for Contact-Rich Manipulation Learning
slides.tldr: TACTILE WEARABLE SYSTEM FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This system uses a wearable device and an isomorphic robot to collect demonstrations of body-surface contact, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on procedural skill acquisition and ego-exo views.

card.one_liner: TWINS enables imitation learning for contact-rich manipulation using a wearable device isomorphic to the execution robot.
card.key_idea: A wearable dual-arm device and isomorphic robot share joint configurations and external dimensions, using distributed tactile sensors to capture body-surface contact for imitation learning.
card.evaluation: Qualitatively evaluated on four tasks (towel hanging, basket holding, ball placing, adaptive holding) using Diffusion Policy; results showed successful phase transitions based on contact.
card.limitation: Occasional failures in holding objects between arm and chest, potentially requiring explicit joint torque control or increased surface compliance.

slides.title: CAAT: Contact-Aware Attention Scaling and Tactile Masking for Data-Efficient Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: IMPROVING VISUO-TACTILE POLICIES VIA CONTACT-AWARE ATTENTION
slides.highlight: CAAT introduces attention scaling and dynamic tactile masking to prioritize visual data before contact and tactile data during contact. This framework improves success rates across various policy architectures in both simulation and real-world contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: CAAT improves contact-rich manipulation by explicitly scaling attention between vision and touch based on contact state.
card.key_idea: A plug-and-play framework using Dynamic Tactile Masking to suppress background noise and Contact-Aware Attention Scaling to prioritize vision before contact and tactile data during contact.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on UniVTAC simulation and real-world tasks using ACT, Diffusion Policy, and π0; CAAT outperformed baselines by up to 21.1 percentage points.

slides.title: EvoHIL: Self-Evolving Reward and Flow-Matched Policy Optimization for Robust Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
slides.highlight: EvoHIL improves robot manipulation through a framework that adapts reward models and stabilizes action generation via flow matching. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EvoHIL improves robust robot manipulation by jointly adapting reward models, action generation, and visual domains.
card.key_idea: Combines self-evolving rewards (SER) for classifier adaptation, flow-matching for temporally coherent action chunks (AFS), and retention-aware offline fine-tuning using relit replay data and network anchors.
card.evaluation: Tested on six manipulation tasks using Franka FR3 and SO-101 arms under lighting shifts; compared against HIL and imitation baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on an external relighter that may not capture all extreme illumination effects or reproduce every visual shift.

slides.title: Semantic Haptic Feedback Enhances Dexterous Robotic Teleoperation
slides.tldr: ABSTRACT HAPTIC PATTERNS IMPROVE BIMANUAL TELEOPERATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces semantic haptics using abstract patterns to convey robot states, reducing hardware constraints and operator workload. It demonstrates superior performance in bimanual tasks compared to sensory and visual feedback.

card.one_liner: Semantic haptic feedback using abstract patterns improves bimanual robotic teleoperation performance and reduces operator workload.
card.key_idea: Replaces raw sensory data with symbolic haptic patterns (confirmations and exceptions) delivered via pneumatic and vibrotactile wristbands to communicate discrete robot state transitions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via three studies in simulation (unimanual and bimanual pick-and-place) against visual and sensory haptics; results showed superior bimanual performance and preference.
card.limitation: The system was evaluated exclusively in a simulated environment to simplify state estimation and focus on haptic design.

slides.title: Demystifying When and Why VLAs Fail in Contact-Rich Tasks and How to Fix Them
slides.tldr: IMPROVING VLA PERFORMANCE IN CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This research identifies precision and force-related failure modes in Vision-Language-Action models and introduces FACT to improve success rates in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: FACT improves VLA performance in contact-rich tasks by addressing precision and force-sensing failure modes.
card.key_idea: Combines a Logit-Normal noise schedule to prioritize fine-correction training with a time-aware force injection mechanism using current readings, history tokens, and gradient gating.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-world tasks via ~2,500 rollouts; FACT achieved 66% average success rate, significantly outperforming ForceVLA (40.5%) and TA-VLA (37.5%).
card.limitation: Tested on one robot platform; LN is specific to flow-matching heads; force injection requires transformer architectures with RMS scaling.

slides.title: A Hierarchical Approach to Imitation Learning for Manipulation Tasks Requiring Time Varying Forces
slides.tldr: HIERARCHICAL DIFFUSION POLICY FOR HIGH-FREQUENCY FORCE REGULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces DPA-FTG, which decouples low-frequency planning from high-frequency force regulation to enable stable contact in dynamic disassembly tasks.
